classification.mathematical_interest: The exact restriction norm is attained by a conformal derivative and becomes asymptotically sharp on a genuine equality family, so it is both a clean Hilbert-space extremal calculation and a quantitatively meaningful geometric consumer.
classification.reusable_scope: Conformal images of fixed interior curves where Euclidean area is the natural $A^2$ norm and a restriction functional can be computed more sharply than generic univalent distortion.
classification.why_it_matters: It turns a loose proof bottleneck into a sharp positive theorem and confines the two-root capacity obligation to a degree-independent neighborhood of the merge level.

primary_sources.title: Metric properties of polynomials
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Problem 5 on page 139 gives the originating short-path question in the polynomial lemniscate.
primary_sources.supports: The historical problem and its metric-polynomial setting.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The Bergman segment estimate, the capacity window, or current numerical reach.

primary_sources.title: A Carleson measure theorem for Bergman spaces
primary_sources.author: William W. Hastings
primary_sources.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 52 (1975), 237-241
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The main theorem characterizes measures supporting norm embeddings from Bergman spaces, establishing the ambient restriction-measure framework.
primary_sources.supports: That Bergman norms against lower-dimensional measures belong to established Carleson-embedding theory.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The exact $A^2$-to-$L^1$ norm on a diameter, its conformal extremal, or the lemniscate application.

primary_sources.title: The areas of polynomial images and pre-images
primary_sources.author: Edward Crane
primary_sources.venue: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 36 (2004), 786-792
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The preimage theorem proves the sharp area bound $\operatorname{Area}(p^{-1}(K))\le\pi^{1-1/n}\operatorname{Area}(K)^{1/n}$; the disk case is identified as Pólya's classical inequality.
primary_sources.supports: The area ceiling $\operatorname{Area}\{|f|<t\}\le\pi t^{2/n}$ used in the source theorem.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The Bergman trace constant or the two-root critical-level reduction.

primary_sources.title: On conformal maps from multiply connected domains onto lemniscatic domains
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 2 states Walsh's lemniscatic-domain theorem and records the Green function and logarithmic-capacity normalization for multiply connected complements.
primary_sources.supports: The conventional Green-function/capacity framework for multiply connected polynomial-preimage geometry.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The exact outside-root additive defect identity or the Bergman two-root consumer.

mechanism_comparison.classical_layer: The disk Bergman kernel represents evaluation, Carleson theory frames restriction measures, Riemann--Hurwitz counts branch points, and Pólya--Crane controls polynomial-preimage area.
mechanism_comparison.exact_local_layer: Kernel positivity on the real diameter makes the constant phase extremal and yields an explicit sharp $L^1$ trace norm with a univalent equality case.
mechanism_comparison.problem_consumer: A degree-two Blaschke representation identifies the descent arc with a conformal diameter, so the exact norm becomes a root-to-root length bound.
mechanism_comparison.capacity_effect: The Pólya area ceiling cancels the degree-dependent scale and leaves the threshold $t/v\ge\coth(1)$.
mechanism_comparison.remaining_throat: The binding limit $t=v$, degenerate multiple critical points, and the near-Fekete equality stratum remain outside the theorem.
